title: Illness on the road and stolen trunks
summary: Henry 'Nick' Turner fell ill in Ashland, Kentucky and the undertaker nearly buried him; Gibson recalls seven trunks of uniforms stolen in Austin and the Thomasville wrecking of instruments.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What about if a guy got sick? And you're on the road.

That's another question. It's hard for me to answer. I don't remember anybody getting sick, but one time was Turner, wasn't it? What about that? Well, that was in later years. But Henry Turner got real sick in a little town of Ashland, Kentucky, I think. It was in the hills. And we had to...no, I'm sorry. Another fellow, Buddy Collins. He was from here. I don't know if you ever hear any talk about him. He was a vocalist. You've told me about him. Yeah. Well, Nick Turner got sick in this little small town in the area. The undertaker wanted to bury him before he died. And we had to leave town. When we came back, we had to take Nick away from there. Because they were getting rid of him faster than where he was supposed to go. But he got over it. We often laugh about that. If we hadn't stayed away a couple of days, old Nick Turner would have been buried over there in Ashland.
I don't know if he's still going or not. You were going to say something?

Well, we've already passed it, but I didn't want to say nothing since you've heard of it. But you said about it being dangerous about the instruments. We played Austin one night, and they didn't steal the instruments there, but they stole seven trunks.
All the clothing. All the uniforms and their regular dress wear.
And that time in Greenland, where they broke your own instruments and the drums and all that?
No, no. I told Nick about that. That's in... Thomasville. Thomasville, Georgia.
Yeah, we were talking about that.
